setName: Cristian Scutaru Book: Practice Exam Questions
domain: Cristian Scutaru Book: Practice Exam Questions

questions.question: You execute a COPY INTO statement to ingest data from a staged file into a table, with VALIDATION_MODE=RETURN_10_ROWS. What happens? (Select Two)

options.text: 10 rows with validation information are returned on screen
First 10 rows from the file will be validated, without loading them into the table
If errors are encountered, the statement will fail at the first error encountered
The statement will continue to validate all 10 rows, even if errors were encountered
If there are no errors, the rows will be loaded into the table

questions.explanation: B and C are correct. COPY INTO is one of the most popular commands in Snowflake, with plenty of clauses and parameters. VALIDATION_MODE=RETURN_10_ROWS validates the first 10 rows from the file without loading them into the table. It's very important to note that with this mode there will be no transfer into the table — it's just about row validation.

questions.question: The Query History page in Snowsight lets you explore queries executed in your Snowflake account for the past:
questions.explanation: B is correct. The Query History page lets you explore queries executed in your Snowflake account over the last 14 days. To monitor query activity, you can also use the QUERY_HISTORY view in the ACCOUNT_USAGE schema of the SNOWFLAKE database, or the QUERY_HISTORY family of table functions in INFORMATION_SCHEMA.

questions.question: Which kind of metadata is saved by Snowflake for each micro-partition? (Select Two)

options.text: Min and max values for each column

questions.explanation: A and C are correct. Snowflake stores metadata about all rows stored in a micro-partition, including the range of values (min/max) for each of the columns in the micro-partition, the number of distinct values, and additional properties used for both optimization and efficient query processing.

questions.question: After you create a scheduled task, what else should you do?

options.text: Run CALL with the name of the task

questions.explanation: B is correct. Any newly created task must be followed by an ALTER TASK with RESUME, if you want to activate it according to the schedule. Otherwise the task remains inactive, and will never trigger an execution. This is important to remember, as it is easy to wrongly assume a task may become active once created.

questions.question: How can you run a query against the cache?

options.text: You call SELECT with the WITH CACHE clause
You find the query in Query History and you re-run it from there
You look for the query identifier with a built-in system function

questions.explanation: C is correct. The system function LAST_QUERY_ID(offset=-1) locates a query with cached result by relative position. Combine it eventually with RESULT_SCAN to get directly the cached result, without running the query again.

questions.question: Which of the following objects can be shared between Snowflake accounts? (Select Three)
questions.explanation: B, C, and D are correct. You can share the following Snowflake objects: Databases, Tables, Dynamic tables, External tables, Iceberg tables, Secure views, Secure materialized views, and Secure user-defined functions (UDFs). File Formats and Resource Monitors cannot be shared.

questions.question: Which of the Snowflake Editions will allow you first to use materialized views?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Materialized views are available starting with the Enterprise Edition. The Enterprise Edition comes with many useful and common features that you don't have in the basic Standard Edition. Business Critical comes with account replication and failover/failback. VPS offers the highest level of isolation and security.

questions.question: What is a Reader Account?

options.text: A special area with inbound shares, for which the provider will pay
A special area with inbound shares, for which the consumer will pay
A separate Snowflake Account with its own billing charge

questions.explanation: A is correct. A Reader Account is not really a separate Snowflake Account. It is an area separated from the Snowflake Account of a provider, who shares read-only data, through inbound shares, with people without their own separate Snowflake Accounts. The provider pays for whatever compute credits the Reader Account will consume.

questions.question: How is the separation of compute and storage working in Snowflake? (Select Two)

options.text: More storage will require more powerful machines
Storage can grow and shrink regardless of the compute power
You can add more compute power without adding more storage
You can specify the compute power and storage required for each virtual warehouse

questions.explanation: B and C are correct. The separation of compute and storage means that the virtual warehouses and the data stored in tables are completely independent. Remote data is completely separated from the virtual warehouses, which are the compute resources. You cannot directly access that data; you do it only through SQL queries.

questions.question: Which of the following apply to a virtual warehouse? (Select Three)

options.text: A warehouse will actually be resized only after the last current query gets executed
You must wait for the last query to execute to resize a warehouse
A warehouse size can be specified only upon creation
A warehouse can auto-resume when new queries need to be executed
A warehouse can be automatically suspended after several minutes of inactivity

questions.explanation: A, D, and E are correct. Each warehouse has optional parameters auto-resume and auto-suspend. You can resize warehouses while active, but only new queries will benefit from the new size. The existing queries must execute, and only then the warehouse will be actually resized. Warehouse size can be changed at any time, not only upon creation.

questions.question: When does it make sense to disable the auto-suspend mode for a virtual warehouse?

options.text: For batch processing, when the compute can be made available later on
When users use the compute sporadically throughout the day
When you manage some steady workloads
When you're the only user with access to that account

questions.explanation: C is correct. Disabling auto-suspend makes sense when you need to permanently keep a warehouse running — when you use it almost constantly with steady workloads, or you don't want to wait for it to wake up for any query. Always use auto-suspend when you query sporadically, with batch jobs, or when you don't have many users in the account.

questions.question: You need to use time travel for 30 days with some tables. What edition would you need?
questions.explanation: B is correct. By default, all editions offer 1-day time travel for any table. This can be increased to max 90 days in the Enterprise edition. The Standard edition is limited to one day max. Manually set it to 0 if you don't want time travel. All permanent tables benefit from 7 days of Fail-safe regardless of edition.

questions.question: How can you load data into a Snowflake table? (Select Three)

options.text: Data loading wizard from the web UI
Snowpipe REST API with continuous loading
Bulk copy from an internal or external stage
COPY INTO a table from a local file
PUT command from a local file directly into a table

questions.explanation: A, B, and C are correct. You can use the data loading wizard in Snowsight, which creates stages, file formats, and runs COPY INTO behind the scenes. Snowpipe can periodically call COPY INTO for continuous loading. Bulk copy uses COPY INTO from a stage. PUT only uploads files to stages, not into tables. COPY INTO transfers data from staged files into tables, not directly from local files.

questions.question: Which of the following tables will automatically be deleted at the end of your session?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Temporary tables are created by you and will be automatically dropped at the end of your session. Unlike permanent tables, transient tables can be used with no Fail-safe. They are also for temporary usage, but can be dropped by any user with access rights and persist beyond the session.

questions.question: Which of the following statements are true? (Select Two)

options.text: You usually pay more for storage when using zero-copy clones
Zero-copy cloned tables are billed separately
A cloned table shares with the original the stored data at the creation time
A zero-copy cloned table is read-only
Changes to cloned data are stored in a separate area

questions.explanation: C and E are correct. When you clone a table, both the original and the clone will share the data at that creation time. After which any other change, in both original or the clone, is saved separately. You pay less in storage for clones, because you don't need to copy the initial data. Cloned tables are not read-only — they are fully writable.

questions.question: Which of the following are blocking statements in Snowflake? (Select Three)
questions.explanation: C, D, and E are correct. UPDATE and DELETE, or even MERGE (which combines INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE) will hold locks that generally prevent them from running in parallel with other similar statements. INSERT will always add new data and doesn't block. UPSERT does not exist as a SQL statement in Snowflake.

questions.question: How many queries can you run in parallel in a virtual warehouse?

options.text: It depends how complex the queries are and how much data they require each
It is based on the MAX_CONCURRENCY_LEVEL parameter
It depends on the client executing the queries

questions.explanation: A is correct. The MAX_CONCURRENCY_LEVEL parameter, by default 8, sets only the maximum number of queries that are allowed to run in parallel. Otherwise, it all depends on the query complexity. You increase the warehouse size for more complex queries, and you use multi-cluster warehouses to improve concurrency (more users accessing the database). Increasing the warehouse size is called (manual) scale-up. Setting up more clusters is called (automatic) scale-out.

questions.question: What minimum privileges do you need to query data from a Snowflake table? (Select Three)

options.text: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE on the table
SELECT on the database and schema
USAGE on the database and schema
USAGE on the warehouse used for the query

questions.explanation: A, D, and E are correct. SELECT on the table is obvious (you don't need INSERT or UPDATE access for read-only). But you also need USAGE privileges on its database and schema. And USAGE on the virtual warehouse you must use to execute the query.

questions.question: Which of the following are part of the access control framework in Snowflake? (Select Two)
questions.explanation: B and C are correct. Snowflake's approach to access control combines aspects from two models: (a) Discretionary Access Control (DAC) — each object has an owner, who can in turn grant access to that object. (b) Role-based Access Control (RBAC) — access privileges are assigned to roles, which are in turn assigned to users.

questions.question: What can FLATTEN be used for?

options.text: For both structured and semi-structured data

questions.explanation: A and B are correct. FLATTEN can be used for both semi-structured data (like JSON arrays and objects) and structured data. When data types like ARRAY or even OBJECT get specific and mandatory data types, their data becomes structured. Snowflake has structured ARRAY and OBJECT types, and MAPs, that can be used in a similar way with FLATTEN.

questions.question: Which type of data integration tools leverage Snowflake's scalable compute for data transformation?
questions.explanation: B is correct. In ETL (Extract-Transform-Load), data is first transformed outside Snowflake, usually in blob storage like S3. An ELT (Extract-Load-Transform) will first load data into Snowflake, then transform it within Snowflake, using its virtual warehouses (the 'compute'), which can scale up or out. Replication is for backup and recovery. Streaming is for near real-time data ingestion.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of consumer accounts that can be added to a share object?
questions.explanation: D is correct. There is no limit to the number of consumer accounts that can be added to a share object, and shared data is always read-only. When in doubt, exclude very low numbers such as 1 or even 10.

questions.question: What technique does Snowflake use to limit the number of micro-partitions scanned by each query?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Pruning is something very specific in Snowflake. When running a query, Snowflake limits scanned data by reading stored metadata — such as the range of values and the count of distinct values — in each micro-partition. This improves query efficiency and response time. Traditional indexes (including B-Tree) did not exist in Snowflake until recently (only for hybrid tables). Map-Reduce is specific to data lakes like Hadoop.

questions.question: Which of the following are options when creating a virtual warehouse? (Select Two)
questions.explanation: A and C are correct. Virtual warehouses can be automatically started (auto-resume) to run queries, and automatically stopped (auto-suspend) after a period of inactivity, to save costs. The most important option is the 'size' of the warehouse. Snowflake doesn't tell us how much RAM, disk space, processors, or cache a machine has. There is no 'default role' for a virtual warehouse.

questions.question: Which role in Snowflake allows a user to administer users and manage all database objects?
questions.explanation: C is correct. There is no ROOT role in Snowflake, and ACCOUNTADMIN is the most powerful role. SECURITYADMIN manages users and roles, and SYSADMIN manages database objects. When you need both capabilities, ACCOUNTADMIN is their common parent and combines the responsibilities of both roles.
